- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.25) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment reversal.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion: if price deviates >2σ from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward MA.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overreacts; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for 5–10 day horizon.
